operations.evidence: Drug-seizure statistics cover the 43 territorial police forces, British Transport Police and Border Force in England and Wales.
The coverage does not include every agency or every seizure outside the defined territory.
Border Force seizures made outside the land territory of England and Wales are excluded from the publication.
Border Force activity totals should not be assumed to represent all UK seizures.
Drug-seizure statistics are presented on a 1 April to 31 March financial-year basis.
Calendar-year comparisons require period alignment.
A seizure involving several drug types is counted once in the overall total and separately for each relevant drug type and class.
Drug-type counts must not be summed to estimate the number of seizure occasions.
Annual movements in quantities can be heavily influenced by a small number of very large seizures.
Quantity changes do not directly measure prevalence or routine local supply.
Drug-seizure statistics are not directly comparable in every year and are not a measure of drug prevalence in society.
Seizure counts must not be converted into parcel-level drug-use estimates.
New psychoactive substance seizures were recorded systematically across police forces and Border Force from the year ending March 2018.
Earlier NPS data are not on the same systematic basis.
GHB, GBL and 1,4-BD were reclassified from Class C to Class B in April 2022, with historical Border Force limitations before 2021.
Class time series require reclassification and source-specific handling.
Nitrous oxide became a Class C drug in November 2023 and older Border Force records are presented under different groupings.
Historical nitrous-oxide categories are not directly homogeneous.
Published figures come from operational records across multiple organisations and are subject to large-system inaccuracies.
Administrative records are not independently observed measures of all drug activity.
Not all seized substances are forensically tested, so some detailed classifications depend on officer identification or offender statements.
Untested substance type must not be treated as laboratory-confirmed.
Most quantity conversion factors have not been updated since 2005, although they are applied consistently through the time series.
Converted dose quantities may be imprecise even when trend treatment is consistent.
Force system changes can produce partial returns, and missing or inaccurate data may be estimated.
Estimated force values must remain distinguishable from observed returns.
New force systems can capture seizure types that older systems omitted, creating apparent increases.
A jump after system migration may reflect coverage change rather than real activity.
Where every cannabis plant cannot be counted, forces may estimate the number of plants seized.
Estimated plant quantities are not exact observations.
Home Office quality assurance checks missing data, inconsistencies, extreme values and invalid quantities and queries unusual trends with forces.
Quality assurance reduces but does not eliminate error.
Imputation is used only when the Home Office and the police force agree it is more accurate than the available data.
Imputed data should not be represented as a direct force record.
Forces can submit revised data and each latest release supersedes the previous release.
Published values require release-date versioning.
International drug-seizure figures may use different periods, counting rules and recording practices.
Cross-country comparisons require harmonised definitions.
Single seizures contain one drug type, while multiple seizures contain two or more types but count once in the total occasion count.
Neither seizure type establishes the exact location, prevalence or risk of a parcel.
The wave46_ source-id prefix had no indexed repository match before publication.
Zero source roles were promoted to exact-address evidence, parcel risk, candidate values or business rows.
100 source rows and 204 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
No second runner, queue replacement, runtime execution, database write or business-data write was performed.
